CITY OF SAN MARINO

  DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA

 Howard Brody, Chair  www.cityofsanmarino.org

 Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair  (626) 300-0711 Phone

  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 20, 2019
  7:00 P.M.
  CITY HALL
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE, SAN MARINO, CA

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design Review Committee
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification
or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705
at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Howard Brody, Vice-Chair Kevin Cheng, Committee Member Judy Johnson-
  Brody, Committee Member Chris Huang, Committee Member Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij,
  and Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200 Huntington
Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation Department, 1560 Pasqualito
Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the Design
Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design Review Committee’s
consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design Review Committee.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – MARCH 20, 2019  PAGE 2 OF 3

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  1. DESIGN REVIEW NO. DRC17-39
  860 ORLANDO RD., (LANGTON INVESTMENT CORP.)
  This item was continued from the meeting of February 6, 2019. The applicant proposes to construct a
  motorized driveway gate, fencing and pilasters in the front yard.
  (Required Action Date: 3-23-19)

  2. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-91
  480 WINTHROP RD., (DABBS)
  This item was continued from the meeting of March 6, 2019. The applicant requests permission to
  construct a front yard fence.
  (Required Action Date: 5-3-19)

  3. DESIGN REVIEW NO. DRC19-7
  2895 WALLINGFORD RD., (WOO)
  The applicant requests to install exterior modifications to the existing one-story structure.
  (Required Action Date: 4-29-19)

  4. DESIGN REVIEW NO. DRC18-90
  3325 MONTEREY RD., (YANG/DIG INC.)
  The applicant requests to construct a first and second-story addition with exterior modifications to the
  existing two-story structure and a new detached three-car garage.
  (Required Action Date: 5-3-19)

  OTHER MATTERS

  5. APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES FOR FEBRUARY 6, 2019 AND MARCH 6, 2019.

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for feedback from
members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited the site and neighborhood.
Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary approval of a project but rather as a tool
in facilitating a project through the Design Review process. No more than two DRC members may participate
in Open Forum discussions. Applications that have been heard by the DRC may not be discussed during Open
Forum.

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design Review Committee
regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200
Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on Wednesday,
April 3, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – MARCH 20, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 3

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the Planning and Building
Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for further information.
   Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Eva Choi, Associate Planner
DATE:  March 20, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC17-39
  860 ORLANDO RD., (LANGTON INVESTMENT CORP.)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a motorized driveway gate, fencing and pilasters with
lighting in the front yard.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15303e because the project involves accessory structures.

PROJECT HISTORY

February 6, 2019 – First hearing before DRC
March 20, 2019 – Second hearing before DRC
March 23, 2019 – Required action date

At the February 6th meeting, the Committee requested confirmation of the property lines to
ensure that the proposed fencing and driveway gate provide the required setback. The applicant
furnished an electronic copy of the property survey to staff on March 13th, however he was not
able to submit revised drawing and survey to the City before the publication of this report. Staff
advised the applicant that he can submit a written request to waive the Permit Streamlining
Act’s timeline and that the Committee continue the hearing to a future date, but no such
request was submitted. Due to the lack of review materials and the impending required action
date, staff recommends denial of Design Review Case Number DRC17-39.
       Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Christine Song, Assistant Planner
DATE:  March 20, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-7
  2895 WALLINGFORD RD., (WOO)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to replace a single door entry with double doors.
The applicant is seeking an after-the-fact approval for new double doors that have already been
installed as part of a previous remodel and addition project.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

March 20, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
April 29, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 6
Object – 0
No response – 6

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:
 1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding:  ☐ YES  ☒ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments:  The legal neighborhood consists of homes in various traditional
  architectural styles with single-door entries. There is one structure in the neighborhood
  with double doors installed, however it is not a good example of an appropriate
  application of double doors. The installation of double doors on the subject home
  produces a modern look that is not compatible with the modest and traditional
  appearance of the neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☐NO  ☒NOT APPLICABLE

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The installed double doors are not compatible with the existing Minimal
  Traditional style home as it is not a typical feature found on this type of structure. The
  frosted glass at the top of the doors and the elongated metal hardware produces a
  contemporary style that is not consistent with the rest of the structure.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: Although the doors’ natural wood composition is a desirable feature, the
  stark black color and opaque laminated glass does not complement the existing
  structure.

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Eva Choi, Associate Planner
DATE:  March 20, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-90
  3325 MONTEREY RD., (YANG/DIG INC.)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a first and second-story addition and remodel with
exterior modifications, and a new detached three-car garage.

The project includes removal of the detached carport, detached guest suite, and trash
enclosure located along the driveway.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) because the project involves an existing structure.

PROJECT HISTORY

March 20, 2019 – First hearing before DRC
May 3, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 4
Object – 0
No response – 4
 DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding:  ☒YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition increases the building height, massing and scale in a manner that
  the structure remains compatible with the legal neighborhood. The existing structure is
  the only Modern Art and Craft/International style in the legal neighborhood and the
  project would maintain this style.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project would not have privacy impacts on adjacent properties. While
  the project includes two balconies on the second floor, there is adequate separation and
  setback to prevent a direct sightline into adjacent structures.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition maintains the asymmetrical façade and varying rooflines. The
  entire structure and the detached garage will be provided with new aluminum clad
  wood windows in a design that is consistent with the architectural style. The project
  also includes skylights which is not uncharacteristic of the modern style.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building
  or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed exterior colors are not overpowering and provide the
  appropriate contrast with the trim colors. The perimeter walls will be repaired and
  repainted to match the proposed stucco color. The balcony railing material will remain
  wrought iron. Dual glazed skylights are proposed over the kitchen and the living room,
  both locations are not visible from street view.

  2

  OF THE SAN MARINO DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE
  FEBRUARY 6, 2019 - 7:00 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER  Chair Brody called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Chair Howard Brody, Vice-Chair Kevin Cheng, Committee Member Judy Johnson- Brody,
  Committee Member Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij, Committee Member Chris Huang, and
  Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren.

ABSENT:  None.

APPEAL PROCEDURE

Chair Brody gave an explanation of the Design Review Committee procedures and explanation of the
fifteen-day appeal procedure to the members of the audience.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

There were no public comments.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  1. DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE CASE NO. DRC18-85
  1539 OAK GROVE AVE., (RYAN/EPT DESIGN)

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody recused herself and stepped out of the Council Chamber.

  Associate Planner Choi presented the project and stated that staff can make the required
  findings to support the project.

  Ross Wooley, project architect, presented the project and answered questions.

  There were no public comments.

  The Committee found the project to be a nice improvement and also compatible with the
  existing structure as well as the neighborhood.

  Vice-Chair Cheng moved to approve the project, with the following conditions of approval:

  1. The glass on the lighting fixture shall be frosted.
  2. Lighting fixtures on the home shall match those on the proposed pilasters.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 6, 2018  PAGE 2

  Second by Committee Member Batnij. AYES: Committee Member Huang, Committee
  Member Batnij, Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair
  Brody. NOES: None.

  2. DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE CASE NO. DRC17-39
  860 ORLANDO RD., (LANGTON INVESTMENT CORP.)

  Associate Planner Choi presented the project and stated that staff needs to request a
  property survey for the project, so a continuance of the project is recommended.

  Vice-Chair Cheng moved to continue the project to the March 20, 2019 meeting.

  Second by Committee Member Huang. AYES: Committee Member Johnson-Brody,
  Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Huang, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody.
  NOES: None.

  3. DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE CASE NO. DRC18-67
  2195 ORLANDO RD., (XU/SLSD)

  Associate Planner Choi presented the project and stated that staff can make the required
  findings to support the project.

  Paula Tsukemoto, project architect, presented the project and answered questions.

  The following person spoke:

  Iris Robin, 2175 Orlando Rd., provided comment in support of the project.

  It was the consensus of the Committee that the project was compatible with the
  neighborhood and the existing structure itself.

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody moved to approve the project as submitted.

  Second by Committee Member Huang. AYES: Committee Member Huang, Committee
  Member Johnson-Brody, and Chair Brody. NOES: Committee Member Batnij and Vice-Chair
  Cheng.

OTHER MATTERS

  4. REQUEST FOR PROJECT APPROVAL EXTENSION
  2605 SYCAMORE DR., (WROBEL, WHITAKER)

  Assistant Planner Song presented the project.

  Bozena Wrobel, property owner, spoke and provided additional background information
  regarding the request.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 6, 2018  PAGE 3

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody moved to approve the extension request with a new
  approval expiration date of August 7, 2019. Second by Committee Member Batnij. AYES:
  Committee Member Huang, Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Johnson-Brody,
  Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

  5. REQUEST FOR PROJECT APPROVAL EXTENSION
  1395 BELHAVEN RD., (JU/TSAO)

  Assistant Planner Song presented the project.

  Vice-Chair Cheng moved to approve the extension request with a new approval expiration
  date of March 21, 2019. Second by Committee Member Johnson-Brody. AYES: Committee
  Member Huang, Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Johnson-Brody, Vice-Chair
  Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

  6. REQUEST FOR PROEJCT APPROVAL EXTENSION
  2458 S. OAK KNOLL AVE., (WANG/HAN)

  Assistant Planner Song presented the project.

  Annie Chiao, daughter of the property owner, spoke on behalf of the property owner and
  provided additional background information regarding the request for the extension.

  Vice-Chair Cheng moved to approve the extension request with a new approval expiration
  date of November 21, 2019. Second by Committee Member Johnson-Brody. AYES:
  Committee Member Huang, Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Johnson-Brody,
  Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

  7. CONSIDERATION OF BORAL MADERA ROOF TILES PRODUCT FOR THE PRE-
  APPROVED ROOF MATERIALS COLORS AND APPLICATION LIST.

  Neal Gochman, Boral representative, presented the roofing material samples and answered
  questions.

  The consensus of the Committee was that the Boral Madera roof tiles are not an acceptable
  roofing material to be placed on the City’s Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and
  Application List, as it would be best to be reviewed on a case by case basis.

  Chair Brody moved not to recommend to the Planning Commission the Boral Madera roof
  tiles for the Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and Application List. Second by Committee
  Member Huang. AYES: Committee Member Huang, Committee Member Johnson-Brody,
  Chair Brody. NOES: Vice-Chair Cheng and Committee Member Batnij.

  8. APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES FOR DECEMBER 5. 2018 AND JANUARY 16, 2019.

  Vice-Chair Cheng moved to approve the minutes as submitted.

  Second by Committee Member Huang. AYES: Committee Member Johnson-Brody,
  Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Huang, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody.
  NOES: None.

With no further items to consider, the DRC adjourned to the next regular Design Review
Committee meeting on Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council

   REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE
  MARCH 6, 2019 - 7:00 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER  Chair Brody called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Chair Howard Brody, Vice-Chair Kevin Cheng, Committee Member Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij,
  Committee Member Chris Huang, Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren, and
  Committee Member Judy Johnson- Brody (arrived at 7:04PM).

ABSENT:  None.

APPEAL PROCEDURE

Chair Brody gave an explanation of the Design Review Committee procedures and explanation of the
fifteen-day appeal procedure to the members of the audience.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

There were no public comments.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  1. DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE CASE NO. DRC18-91
  480 WINTHROP RD., (DABBS)

  Assistant Planner Song stated that the project designer was hospitalized and was not able to
  submit the project drawings for review. Assistant Planner Song recommended that the project
  be continued to the march 20, 2019 meeting.

  There were no public comments.

  Committee Member Huang moved to continue the project to the March 20, 2019 meeting.

  Second by Committee Member Batnij. AYES: Committee Member Huang, Committee
  Member Batnij, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody entered the Council Chamber.

  2. DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE CASE NO. DRC18-89
  2235 MELVILLE DR., (WEI/SLSD INC.)

  Associate Planner Choi presented the project and stated that staff can make the required
  findings for compatibility of the front porch but has concern with the use of fiberglass and
  polyvinyl chloride material for the new shutters.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MARCH 6, 2019  PAGE 2

  David Lai and Perry Chan, project designers, explained the reasons for using the fiberglass and
  polyvinyl chloride material for the shutters and passed along a sample shutter to demonstrate
  that the material closely mimics the appearance of natural wood.

  There were no public comments.

  It was the consensus of the Committee that the project is compatible with the neighborhood
  and with the structure itself. The Committee found the shutter material acceptable but was
  concerned with the proposed metal canopy over the front porch and the size of the shutters.

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody moved to approve the project with the following
  conditions of approval:

  1. New shutter size shall match or be larger than existing shutters.
  2. Paint color on the pedestrian and driveway gates and the adjoining columns shall be white
  trim or painted in the same color as the proposed light grey stucco color.
  3. Work with staff on an appropriate material to cover the portico that will either be copper
  or matching the same roof material on the residence.

  Second by Vice-Chair Cheng. AYES: Committee Member Johnson-Brody, Committee Member
  Batnij, Committee Member Huang, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

OTHER MATTERS

  3. CONSIDERATION OF JELD-WEN CUSTOMTM WOOD SERIES WINDOW MATERIAL FOR
  THE PRE-APPROVED WINDOW MATERIAL LIST.

  Assistant Planner Song presented the proposal and introduced the Jeld-Wen company
  representative.

  Colleen Yee, Jeld-Wen representative, presented the window samples and answered
  questions.

  It was the consensus of the Committee that the Jeld-Wen CustomTM Wood Series window
  material is a good quality product and an acceptable window material for the City’s Pre-
  Approved Window Material list.

  Committee Member Johnson-Brody moved to recommend the Jeld-Wen CustomTM Wood
  Series window material to the Planning Commission for approval with the following
  conditions:

  1. Only the window options on the “Trim & Divided Lites” page of the provided brochure,
  without grills between the divided lites, would be eligible for the Pre-Approved Window
  Material list.
  2. Window replacements shall match existing windows on the structure.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
MARCH 6, 2019  PAGE 3

  Second by Vice-Chair Cheng. AYES: Committee Member Batnij, Committee Member Johnson-
  Brody, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: Committee Member Huang.

  4. CONSIDERATION OF DAVINCI SIMULATED SHAKE AND SLATE ROOFING PRODUCTS
  FOR THE PRE-APPROVED ROOF MATERIALS COLORS AND APPLICATION LIST.

  Assistant Planner Song presented the proposal and introduced the DaVinci company
  representative.

  Scott Fury, DaVinci representative, presented the roofing material samples and answered
  questions.

  It was the consensus of the Committee that the DaVinci roofing product is an attractive
  alternative to natural slate roofing material and would be an acceptable material for the City’s
  Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and Application list.

  Chair Brody moved to recommend the DaVinci roofing product to the Planning Commission
  for approval with the following conditions:

  1. The Multi-Width Slate, the Single-Width Slate, and the Multi-Width Shake only in the
  colors noted with an asterisk (*) on the provided brochures shall be placed on the Pre-
  Approved Roof Materials Colors and Application list.

  Second by Vice-Chair Cheng. AYES: Committee Member Huang, Committee Member Batnij,
  Committee Member Johnson-Brody, Vice-Chair Cheng, and Chair Brody. NOES: None.

ADJOURNMENT

With no further items to consider, the DRC adjourned to the next regular Design Review
Committee meeting on Wednesday, March 20, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers,
2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, CA 91108.

  EVA CHOI,
  ASSOCIATE PLANNER
